memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Be careful that you do not forget the Lord your God, failing to observe his commands, his laws and his decrees that I am giving you this day. Otherwise, when you eat and are satisfied, when you build fine houses and settle down, and when your herds and flocks grow large and your silver and gold increase and all you have is multiplied, then your heart will become proud and you will forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt, out of the land of slavery. - Deut 8:11-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses names a real and subtle danger: forgetting God in the good times. He traces the downward path step by step. First comes satisfaction — full stomachs, fine houses, growing wealth. Then comes a proud heart. And finally comes forgetting God altogether. It is a slow, quiet slide, and it begins not in obvious rebellion but in the comfort of blessing. Prosperity, if we are not careful, can lull the soul to sleep.

This is one of the great spiritual dangers, and it is worth taking seriously. When life is hard, we lean on God; when life is easy, we can drift from Him without even noticing. Comfort has a way of making us feel self-sufficient. We begin to think we built our lives ourselves, that we are secure because of our own efforts, and slowly God fades into the background. The very blessings meant to make us grateful can make us proud and forgetful instead.

The remedy is intentional remembering. Moses does not tell them to avoid prosperity, but to be careful within it — to keep remembering the Lord who rescued them from slavery. For us, the antidote to a proud, forgetful heart is to keep the gospel at the center: to remember constantly that we were slaves to sin, rescued not by our own effort but by the blood of Christ. Success is not the enemy; forgetting God is. Guard your heart in the good times as watchfully as in the hard ones, and keep remembering the One who saved you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Am I more likely to drift from God in comfort than in hardship?
- Where might prosperity or success be quietly making me proud or forgetful?
- How can I intentionally keep remembering God in the good times?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, guard my heart from the danger of forgetting You in times of comfort and success. Keep me humble and grateful, always remembering that I was rescued not by my own effort but by the blood of Christ. Amen.
